entry.content:

Implementing undo and redo functionality requires managing software state changes through specific data structures and user experience design. Developers typically employ a pair of stacks—an undo stack and a redo stack—to handle action history in a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) manner. By popping actions from the undo stack and pushing them onto the redo stack, applications allow users to navigate through a reversible history of changes.

The technical requirements vary by application type, with text editors requiring significantly less overhead than bitmap graphics programs. Text editors can store simple character changes, whereas bitmap editors must often take snapshots of large segments of image data to allow for pixel-level restoration. This creates a trade-off between the depth of the undo history and the consumption of system memory and disk space.

entry.title: C2PA Specification Vulnerability Enables Timestamped Content Tampering
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | da.vidbuchanan.co.uk | discussion

A vulnerability in the C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) specification allows for file content to be altered after signing without invalidating cryptographic signatures or Time Stamp Authority (TSA) timestamps. By leveraging the "exclusions" feature—which allows specific byte ranges to be omitted from signature calculations—a user can exclude the entire file and sign an empty string. This results in a valid, timestamped signature that covers no data, permitting subsequent modification of the file's contents.

The "exclusion" mechanism is a feature of the C2PA specification designed to accommodate file formats that require post-signature changes, such as updating CRC32 checksums in PNG files. Because current verification tools do not typically flag or restrict the size of these exclusion ranges, the technique allows for the creation of forged, timestamped media. A proposed mitigation involves requiring verifiers to enforce strict, format-specific constraints on which portions of a file are permitted to be excluded from a signature.

entry.content:

Trail of Bits has introduced SequenceHash and SequenceMAC, cryptographic constructions designed for secure multihashing across various hash functions. These tools prevent vulnerabilities caused by ambiguous input encoding and length-extension attacks, which occur when multiple data inputs are concatenated before being hashed. Unlike NIST’s TupleHash, which is tied to Keccak, SequenceHash is hash-agnostic and supports algorithms such as the SHA2 family and BLAKE.

The constructions use a double-hash architecture and a 128-bit length-suffix encoding to ensure semantic distinction between inputs and provide resistance to length-extension. SequenceMAC offers a keyed variant with built-in customization strings for domain separation and protection against key pseudocollisions. Implementations are available in Rust, Go, and Python, and the specification is part of the Community Cryptography Specification Project (C2SP).

entry.title: Docker and OCI Layers Handle File Deletions via Whiteout Files
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | loige.co | discussion

Docker and OCI image layers operate as immutable, tar-based filesystem changesets. Because the tar format cannot natively express the deletion of a file, the OCI specification uses "whiteout" files (prefixed with `.wh.`) to instruct container runtimes to hide files or directories from preceding layers.

This mechanism includes "opaque whiteouts" (`.wh..wh..opq`), which allow a layer to hide all children of a directory from previous layers, effectively resetting the directory's contents. These whiteout files are an OCI convention interpreted by the runtime during layer application rather than a native feature of the tar archive format.

entry.title: Futhark Introduces #[cpu_function] Attribute for Mixed CPU and GPU Execution
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | futhark-lang.org | discussion

The Futhark programming language has introduced a #[cpu_function] attribute to allow specific functions to run on the CPU within GPU-accelerated programs. This feature addresses performance bottlenecks caused by inherently sequential algorithms, such as graph coloring, which perform poorly when executed on GPU hardware. The attribute ensures that a function's body and its internal arrays are managed in CPU memory, with the final result being copied back to GPU memory to maintain compatibility with subsequent parallel tasks.

This implementation provides a practical workaround for Futhark's current compilation model, which typically allocates all arrays to a single memory space—usually GPU memory—when using a GPU backend. By enabling efficient CPU-based execution for sequential logic, the language can better handle complex pre-processing steps for highly parallelizable numerical computations. The development team envisions a future where the compiler automatically manages data placement between CPU and GPU memory based on usage patterns.

entry.content:
Lobsters Top | rahuljuliato.com | discussion

A Domain-Specific Language (DSL) for JavaScript and TypeScript enables the creation of readable regular expressions by modeling them as a tree of named, composable forms, a technique inspired by the Emacs `rx` macro. This approach simplifies the maintenance of complex patterns, such as Semantic Versioning strings, by replacing opaque, single-line regex literals with structured code.

The implementation utilizes a custom `RxNode` structure to manage literals, character sets, and sequences, automating much of the escaping and grouping logic. It supports named capturing groups, greedy and lazy repetitions, and provides a `raw` function to integrate existing regular expressions into the DSL structure.

entry.title: Outis Generates Fake Bounce Emails to Combat Spam
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion

Outis is an open-source command-line tool that generates fake "user unknown" bounce emails to combat spam. By sending an RFC 3464 delivery status notification to the sender, the tool makes the recipient's address appear non-existent, helping to remove the address from automated or AI-generated mailing lists.

The tool is most credible when used with an SMTP account from a domain the user controls, as consumer email providers often rewrite headers and can expose the user. While it does not prevent the initial spam from being delivered, the resulting notification is designed to trick automated systems into thinking the mailbox is invalid.

entry.title: Linux Support for Apple M4 Chips Enabled via WFI Workaround
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | yuka.dev | discussion

Technical challenges have emerged in booting Linux on Apple's M4 SoC due to a non-compliant implementation of the WFI (Wait For Interrupt) instruction. This hardware behavior causes the loss of CPU architectural state, preventing stable multi-core operation during low-power transitions.

A workaround involving the replacement of WFI instructions with NOPs or the use of specific kernel boot arguments has been merged into the mainline Linux kernel and the m1n1 bootloader. This enables full multi-core functionality on M4, M4 Pro, M4 Max, and M5 Apple Silicon chips, while reverse-engineering of remaining peripherals like the GPU remains ongoing.
